info.name: Aastrika Common Service
info.description:
All API endpoints for aastrika-common-service, grouped by controller: Certificate, Passbook, Leaderboard, Ratings.

Usage:
1. Import into Postman. The collection id is kept stable, so re-importing this file updates your existing collection in place (choose Replace if prompted) rather than creating a new one.
2. Set the collection variable `baseUrl` (default http://localhost:7011).
3. Requests carry test assertions on the expected HTTP status. In the Passbook folder, run 'Add entries' before the 'Duplicate add' error case.

request.description: Completion + certificate-generated status for (rootOrgId, programId, userId). 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND if no completion row exists (Postgres user_program_completion).
Resolves the downloadable certificate URL. 404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND / 400 PROGRAM_NOT_COMPLETED / 404 CERTIFICATE_NOT_GENERATED depending on state.
Adds passbook entries for `userId` (from the body). The header user is stored as `createdBy`.
Reads the authenticated user's own passbook. The user comes from the `x-authenticated-userid` header.
Reads passbooks for a list of users. No auth header required; users come from the body.

item.name: Ratings
item.description:
The four implemented RatingsController endpoints. The meta-update and additional-tag ops jobs were removed as unused.

Notes:
- R1 (upsert) writes to Cassandra AND emits a Kafka event to dev.rating.event.
- R1/R3/R4/R5 share collection variables pointing at a verified-enrolled user+activity, so the aggregation actually completes. An unenrolled pair is silently dropped to the DLQ (see R10).
- R1 varies the rating each run: a zero delta is a no-op in the aggregation.

exec: // The aggregation is delta-based: it only touches ratings_summary when the rating
// actually CHANGES. Re-posting the same value is a silent no-op, so cycle 1..5 to
// guarantee a non-zero delta on every run.
// The rating row is written synchronously; the summary is updated by the Kafka
// consumer, so give it a moment before running R4.

body.raw:
{
  "activityId": "{{ratingActivityId}}",
  "activityType": "{{ratingActivityType}}",
  "userId": "{{ratingUserId}}",
  "rating": {{ratingValue}},
  "review": "This course was genuinely useful and clearly structured. The examples were easy to follow and the pacing felt right across every module.",
  "recommended": "yes"
}

request.description:
Create/update a rating. Emits a Kafka event unless it's a comment-only update.

Uses a verified-enrolled user: the aggregator drops events for users with no row in sunbird_courses.user_enrolments, so an unenrolled pair leaves the summary empty forever (see R10). The pre-request script varies the rating because a zero delta is a no-op.
Ratings for one activity across a list of users.

exec: // A missing summary row still returns 200 with response=null, which is easy to mistake
// for success. Assert it is populated so a dropped aggregation event fails loudly.
"null summary - the aggregation event was probably DLQ'd, check the consumer log"

request.description:
Star counts + latest reviews (enriched with reviewer first name).

Returns 200 with response=null when no ratings_summary row exists. Reviews only appear in latest50reviews when longer than 100 chars (REVIEW_MIN_LENGTH).

exec: // To paginate: take the last item's updatedOnUuid and send it as 'updateOn' next call.

request.description: Paginated reviews. Optional 'rating' filters by star; 'updateOn' is the cursor (updatedOnUuid of the last row).
rating must be between 1 and 5.

item.name: R10. Upsert by NON-enrolled user -> 200, but aggregation drops it

exec: pm.test("status is 200 (the upsert itself succeeds)", () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
// Deliberately NOT asserting on the summary: this request exists to show that a 200
// here does not mean the aggregation ran.

request.description:
Regression guard for the trap that this endpoint returns 200 either way.

The rating row IS written, but the consumer throws NotEnrolledException (RatingAggregationServiceImpl:57), which is non-retryable, so the event goes straight to rating.failedRating and ratings_summary/ratings_lookup are never touched. Nothing in the HTTP response hints at this - check the consumer log or the DLQ depth.

item.name: Assessment
item.description:
POST /v2/user/assessment/submit — the only consumed assessment endpoint. Scoring is in-memory (the answer key rides in the request: each option carries isCorrect + the user's userSelected/response). Returns the raw score summary with HTTP 201 (NOT the AppResponse envelope — preserved for the live client contract).

External calls: user validation (user-search) and content hierarchy (getParent/getContentType). For local testing point user.search-url at the mock (scripts/mock-content-service.py) and content.hierarchy-url at the real content service.

exec: pm.test("has score fields", () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b).to.have.property("result"); pm.expect(b).to.have.property("correct"); pm.expect(b).to.have.property("total"); });

request.description: 1 correct + 1 incorrect + 1 blank -> result 33.33. Writes user_quiz_master + user_quiz_summary.
Writes user_assessment_master. The user_assessment_summary row is only written when the identifier's parent resolves to a Course (parentContentType == 'course').
userId 'invalid-user' -> the mock user-search returns count 0 -> 'Invalid UserId.' 400. (Against a real user service, use any non-existent userId.)
Body missing the required 'identifier' -> bean validation 400.

item.name: Mandatory Content
item.description: Mandatory-content status check migrated from sunbird-cb-ext. Requires a live Cassandra (sunbird.mandatory_user_content) and course service; not mock-backed.

header.description: Course-service token (source header name). Replace with a fresh token when expired.

request.description: Whether the user has completed every mandatory course for their org. Reads sunbird.mandatory_user_content (needs rows for root_org/org) and calls the course-service progress read per course — point COURSE_SERVICE_HOST at your real course service. Uniform envelope: result.response = {mandatoryCourseCompleted, contentDetails}. Header 'xAuthUser' token expires — paste a fresh one.

item.name: Profile
item.description:
ProfileController: OpenSearch user autocomplete, admin org migration, and the user bulk-upload job APIs.

WARNING - PR2 (migrate) is DESTRUCTIVE and NOT atomic. Step 1 calls the learner service and is irreversible once it succeeds, even if the later profiledetails rewrite, PUBLIC-role assignment or data-sync fail. Point migrateUserId at a disposable account only; migrateChannel must be the channel of a TENANT org (sunbird.organisation.istenant = true) or the learner service rejects it.

PR3 needs a file attached by hand - Postman stores only a local path for form-data files, so the collection cannot ship one. Attach an .xlsx whose first row is exactly: firstname | lastname | email | phone. The row cap is bulk-upload.max-rows (default 2000). PR3's test script writes the returned jobId into the bulkJobId collection variable, so run PR3 before PR5 and PR6.

PR1 needs a reachable OpenSearch at sb.lern.es.host.list; PR2-PR6 need PostgreSQL, and PR2 additionally needs Cassandra plus the learner service.

request.description:
Prefix search over the OpenSearch user index (sb.lern.es.user.profile.index, default user_alias). Matches the fields in es.user.auto.complete.search.fields (firstName.raw, email.raw, lastName.raw) and returns the _source fields listed in es.user.auto.complete.include.fields.

Envelope: result.response = {content: [...], count: n}. No auth header - the gateway is expected to have authenticated the caller. Any ES failure surfaces as 500 with params.errmsg.

item.name: PR2. Migrate user to another org (PATCH /user/v1/migrate)  -- DESTRUCTIVE

header.description: Constants.X_AUTH_TOKEN - forwarded verbatim to the learner service.
Constants.AUTH_TOKEN - forwarded verbatim to the learner service.

request.description:
DESTRUCTIVE AND NOT ATOMIC. Five steps in order: (1) learner-service org migration - irreversible once it returns success, (2) read sunbird.user, (3) rewrite profiledetails and write it back with the new channel, (4) assign the PUBLIC role against rootorgid, (5) trigger a data-sync. A failure in steps 2-5 leaves the user already migrated at step 1.

The source's {"request": {...}} envelope is kept deliberately - admin tooling calls this, so the wire contract must stay byte-compatible.

Status codes diverge from the source's blanket 500: 404 missing user, 422 unusable profileDetails, 502 downstream failure. An invalid channel is reported by the learner service and surfaced verbatim as 502.

item.name: PR3. Bulk upload users (POST /user/v1/bulkupload)  -- attach an .xlsx

header.description: Constants.X_AUTH_USER_ORG_ID - the rootOrgId the job and its rows are filed under.

formdata.description: Attach an .xlsx. The header row must be exactly: firstname | lastname | email | phone. Postman cannot ship the file inside the collection, so select one here before sending.

request.description:
Parses the sheet in memory, runs the CPU-only validations, persists a job plus one row per line, and returns immediately - user creation happens afterwards off the PENDING rows. The file itself is not retained; the per-row state is the record of the upload.

Envelope: result = {jobId, fileName, status: INITIATED, totalRecords, validRecords, invalidRecords, invalidRows: [{rowNumber, errors}]}.

400 if the file is empty, unreadable, not a .xlsx, has the wrong header, has no data rows, or exceeds bulk-upload.max-rows (default 2000).

The test script writes jobId into the bulkJobId collection variable for PR5 and PR6.

item.name: PR4. Upload history for an org (GET /user/v1/bulkupload/{orgId})

request.description: The org's upload history, newest first. Envelope: result = {count, content: [...]}, each entry {jobId, fileName, status, totalRecords, validRecords, invalidRecords, pendingRecords, successfulRecords, failedRecords, createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt} - the per-status counts are derived from the stored rows, not cached on the job.

item.name: PR5. Upload detail, FAILED rows only (GET /user/v1/bulkupload/{orgId}/{jobId})

query.description: Optional. PENDING | INVALID | SUCCESS | FAILED, case-insensitive. Drop it to see every row.

request.description:
One job with its rows. This replaces the source's re-uploaded annotated spreadsheet - filter by status instead of downloading a marked-up sheet.

Envelope: the job summary fields plus result.records = [{rowNumber, firstName, lastName, email, phone, status, errors, updatedAt}].

Needs bulkJobId, which PR3 sets. 404 if the job does not belong to that org.

exec: pm.test('reports how many rows were re-queued', () => pm.expect(b.result.requeuedRecords).to.be.a('number'));

request.description:
Returns the job's FAILED rows to PENDING and re-queues it. INVALID rows are deliberately left alone - their data is wrong, so they need a corrected sheet rather than a retry.

Envelope: result = {jobId, status: INITIATED, requeuedRecords}. requeuedRecords is 0 when nothing had failed. 404 if the job does not belong to that org.

item.name: Profile - Errors
item.description: Negative cases for the Profile endpoints. All three are safe to run - none of them reaches the irreversible learner-service migration call.

item.name: PR7. Migrate with blank channel -> 400 (bean validation)

request.description: channel is @NotBlank on the nested payload, so @Valid rejects this at the controller boundary - the learner service is never called, which is why this one is safe to run. The source validated the envelope by hand and returned 500; bean validation turns that into a proper 400.

item.name: PR8. Bulk upload a non-xlsx file -> 400

formdata.description: Attach any non-.xlsx file (a .csv, a .txt, an old .xls). Expect: 'The file could not be read as a .xlsx workbook'.

request.description: A .csv, .xls or arbitrary bytes all fail the same way - the parser opens the upload as an XSSFWorkbook and a failure there is reported as 400 rather than leaking the POI exception. Sending no file at all yields 'The uploaded file is empty'.

item.name: PR9. Upload detail for an unknown jobId -> 404

request.description: The lookup is scoped by org, so this is also what a caller sees when the job exists but belongs to a different org - a deliberate 404 rather than a 403, so job ids are not enumerable across orgs. A jobId that is not a UUID gives 400 instead, from the PathVariable conversion.

Drop-in replacement for the recommendation service's /publicSearch/getcourse. Unauthenticated: no X-Auth-User-Id. Response is the RAW payload {"results":{"content":[...],"totalCount":n}} — deliberately NOT the AppResponse envelope, so existing callers switch host only. `resourceType`, `sorting_fieldname` and `primaryCategory` are accepted and ignored; results are always sorted by lastUpdatedOn desc.

item.name: P2. Course search — filters only (blank search_text)

request.description: Blank search_text drops the multi_match and returns every Live course of the given contentType, newest first. limit defaults to 25 when omitted or <= 0.
A non-blank language adds a match on the index's `lang` field on top of the text/filter clauses.
course_status and contentType are @NotBlank. Unlike the success path, validation/upstream errors DO use the AppResponse error envelope (params.errmsg).
